title: Disrupting a Russian Influence Campaign
hook: OpenAI banned Russia-origin accounts using its models to prop up a fake Israel-based think tank and a 'sovereignty' index that flattered Russia and dinged the West.
key_points: OpenAI reports banning accounts of Russian origin conducting a covert influence operation.
The operation fabricated an Israel-based think tank as a front for its output.
It also published a 'sovereignty' index constructed to praise Russia and criticize Western countries.
The pattern is content-generation at scale wrapped in a fabricated institutional identity to borrow credibility.
Disclosure reports like this are a main public window into how state-linked actors actually use commercial models.
content_html: OpenAI published an account of banning a cluster of Russia-origin accounts running a covert influence operation on its platform. The campaign promoted a fabricated Israel-based think tank and circulated a "sovereignty" index engineered to praise Russia and criticize Western countries.
extra_html:
The shape of the misuse

What stands out is not the text generation — that part is easy — but the packaging. Anonymous content persuades poorly; content attributed to a research institute, complete with an index and a methodology, borrows the credibility of a genre readers already trust. The model does the volume, the fake institution does the laundering.

Why the report matters

Only the provider can see account-level behaviour, so these disclosures are most of the public record on how state-linked actors use commercial models. They come with obvious selection bias: a lab reports the operations it caught, on its own platform, with framing it chooses. Read them as evidence of tactics rather than as a measurement of scale.

related.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
related.hook: Most pretraining-poisoning research injects fake Wikipedia edits — a toy case next to messy web-scale reality. This paper shows public discussion forums are a real, live vector for attacking LLM pretraining data.

related.title: Grokipedia vs Wikipedia: An LLM-Based Audit of Political Neutrality along Ideologies
related.hook: Grokipedia launched as the 'unbiased' answer to Wikipedia's alleged left-lean. Audited by four LLM judges, including Grok itself, it rates less neutral — just biased the other way.

related.title: A Model's Stance Is a Deployment Setting, Not a Property
related.hook: The same Grok model ID rated a pseudo-scientific claim 75 via API and 5.5 via web. What a commercial LLM 'believes' turns out to be a contingent effect of how it's deployed.

flashcards.prompt: What role did the fake think tank play in this operation?
flashcards.back_html: It supplied institutional cover — model-generated content published under a fabricated Israel-based organization borrows credibility that anonymous posts would not have.

flashcards.prompt: Why are lab disruption reports a useful source on AI misuse?

choices.text: They are one of the few public windows into how state-linked actors actually use commercial models
They quantify the total volume of misuse across all providers
They are independently audited before publication
They prove the campaigns had no measurable effect

flashcards.explanation_html: Only the provider sees the account-level activity, so its own disclosures — with all the selection bias that implies — are most of the public record.
